12. But whether the certified copy is prepared by the office or is supplied by a party comparison with the original copy is a must. Whether this comparison was made in this case has not been stated by the person who purportedly certified it. Mr. Asrarul Hossain has contended that when an oriental document is lost secondary evidence thereof is admissible and it shall be presumed to be correct, as provided in section 74 of the Evidence Act. This presumption is, however, rebuttable, and the presumption is as to regularity of the official act and not as to the correctness of its contents. Again, when a certified copy of the amended Articles of Association was filed by respondent No. I as an Annexure to his affidavit-in-opposition (page 130 on 1-12-75) in the court the last page containing Serial Number One was taken off. No satisfactory explanation has been offered by him as to why this part of the document was withheld Mr. Khondkar contends that the only reason for this omission is that the respondent No. I intended to keep this "discrepancy" out of the notice of the court as well as of the petitioner Respite No .1 subsequently filed the full copy, Ext. 10 containing the last page but it has been kept in the Exhibit File. A document which is the part of a petitions or affidavit in opposition is ordinarily referred to by the court as it is oar at hand in preference to a document kept in the Pat. File. Discrepancy as to the Serial Number of Ext. 10 and subsequent withholding of the last page bearing this number from the court unerringly indicate that the authenticity of the certified copy is doubtful. 

 "It is possible to come to any such definite finding that such fraud was actually practiced upon the petitioner. It only proves an imprudent action on the part of the petitioner showing his lack of common sense in dealing with the affairs of the management of the company. Although brothers might have familiar family relationship as such, but such smooth relationship cannot be the basis of any presumption while 	managing the affairs of any company. No specific remedy in this regard is available in this proceeding under Companies Act while considering the legality or the propriety for 	making any order for winding up of any company. We do not think that the learned Single Judge was justified in keeping the question undecided for this question touches at the root of the mutual confidence of two brothers who were the only two shareholders of the company at the relevant time The petitioner not only brought the allegation of usurpation of all powers by the respondent but also deposed that be got no confidence in the Managing Director of the Company, and if fraud has been practiced by the latter it has cut at the, root of the Company.
